description: We’re building an interactive web tool that makes SPHEREx sky observations easier to explore and compare over time. By turning complex astronomical data into clear visual experiences, we help people spot changes in the sky and discover objects that might otherwise go unnoticed. Our goal is to make space exploration more accessible, intuitive, and engaging for everyone.
summary: SimpleSpace is a user-friendly, on-line time lapse sky viewing tool created to assist Citizen Scientists and Astronomers in finding moving astronomical objects (e.g., Brown Dwarfs, Comets, Planet X Candidates) in NASA's SPHEREx data. Every 6 months, SPHEREx will produce over a billion objects within 102 near-infrared spectral bands, which will be in the form of very large, noisy FITS files that are hard for volunteers to examine by eye. SimpleSpace allows users to turn any sky coordinates (RA, Dec) into an immediate multi-epoch animation. Users have the option of turning on/off frame subtraction (Diff mode) so static stars disappear from view and moving targets become visible, combining all 17 spectral channels for each detector to increase image quality (SNR) by 4.1 times and then click on any target to see its complete 102-band 1D spectrum right away. Our automated Python pipeline downloads small cutout images through IRSA APIs and AWS S3 (which reduces data transfer by 50x), removes 22 types of artifacts such as cosmic rays, satellite trails, zodiacal dust, and matches all detected sources with over 3 billion stars from Gaia DR3, AllWISE, and CatWISE2020. With 24/7 weekly releases and shareable URLs (?ra=...&dec=...), SimpleSpace allows more than 100,000 volunteer scientists using Backyard Worlds to find new things in the universe faster.
details:
Functionality and Operational Mechanism

• Continuous celestial time-lapse. Users enter appropriate celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), as well as Field of View, resulting in generation of an interactive flipbook-style animation around SPHEREx QR3 and DR1 releases.

• Epoch subtraction movement (diffusion mode). Our pipeline overlays exposures via WCS projection into common spatial grid and derives the difference between later epochs and earlier ones (Epoch N – Epoch 1). Static stars in the background disappear, leaving moving or changing objects visible as dipoles.

• Application of 6 detectors and one-dimensional spectroscopy. Users can combine images from all 17 SPHEREx spectral channels from 6 available LVF detectors (D1 to D6 with a range of 0.75 to 5.00 μm) in order to increase image quality (improved SNR by about 4.1 times), or click on a specific target and obtain a full 102-band infrared spectrum available at that moment.

• 24/7 automatic discovery. Background worker works with IRSA releases on a weekly basis through planeid launch and automatically processes the recent frames in order to detect the presence of the new candidate objects NEW_CANDIDATE and PROPER_MOTION_SHIFT.

Advantages and Expected Benefits

• Up to 50 times less needed bandwidth and playback in less than a second. Instead of downloading huge MEF full frame
